holiday.action: A FEEL day in Cancer season — THE TIDE WITHIN.

soulQuestions: Where in your body does homesickness for a place that never existed live? Sit with the ache for the home you deserved instead of the one you got — no fixing, no redecorating. Just feel what's underneath the longing.
What memory do you keep perfectly preserved because admitting how it actually felt would mean the house you grew up in was never as safe as you needed it to be?
adventures: Cook one meal exactly the way it was made for you as a kid — no upgrades, no health swaps. Serve it to someone and tell them the story while you eat.
Before your phone, your list, or anyone's opinion: write down what your gut says about one live decision today. Seal it. Check back in a week and grade the gut, not the outcome.

soulQuestions: Set one boundary that protects your tenderness instead of your pride: a door that closes, a phone that sleeps in another room, a 'not tonight' with no twelve-page explanation. Guard the soft thing, not the image.
Whose feelings have you been treating as weather you must manage, when your gut has been quietly telling you those storms were never yours to calm?

Fix one small corner of your home so it works for the life you actually live — the chair nobody sits in, the drawer that fights back. One corner. Done by tonight.

holiday.name: Cancer Season · THINK
holiday.action: A THINK day in Cancer season — THE TIDE WITHIN.

soulQuestions: You remember everything — every slight filed, every kindness catalogued. Which memory are you curating like evidence for a trial nobody scheduled? Decide today: is it protection, or a grudge with excellent record-keeping?
Is your home a place you built for living, or a fortress you built so nobody could ask you to come out and live?
adventures: Fix one small corner of your home so it works for the life you actually live — the chair nobody sits in, the drawer that fights back. One corner. Done by tonight.
Stand physically, literally between someone you love and one hard thing today — make the call, take the meeting, lift the box. Then step back and let them live their own life.
